If you are playing only 2-player games, a lot of defenses go flying out
the window (notably bleed-bounce (using Deflections) and _possibly_
offensive vote-race (using damage votes to kill before killed)).

What kind of environment do you play with? Pure (by the Rulebook) Jyhad,
Duelist Convocation Tournament Rules, something else? These questions are
important. Have you been trading yet? With so few cards, its hard to
build a balanced deck without trading.

Hope to hear from you.

rob...@adam.com.au (robert donoghue) writes:

>I've bought about 3 decks, 5 boosters (so what can i say? ive only been
>in this 2 weeks...)
>my friends got a good malk deck and bleeds the sh*t out of me. I got
>seven(yep, 7) auspex cards, no Radio Station or sports bikes, so
>blocking's not so flash. Any ideas? (2 Malks and no Ventrue, so bleeding
>him is out of the picture...)

Sounds like your playing a two-player game. If so, try getting more
players.

Other defenses:
Bounce (use deflection and/or Telemathic Misdirection) - only useful in
a three-or-more-player-game.
Combat: Stock some Bum's Rushes and Haven Uncovereds (and Archon, if you
have them and can pass the vote), and beat his bleeders into torpor
and then bleed him at you leisure.
Protected Resources (a rare card).
Archon Investigation (an uncommon card).

bleeding
>him is out of the picture...)

As L. Scott Johnson states it appears that a good combat rush deck might
be the best offense. Also try some Pulled Fangs. If you do more damage
at close range than your opponent you can pull a fang. For starters this
does 1 pt aggravated to them. I normally save this card for after I've
knocked them to zero blood, and a pulled fang simply burns them out of
the game. Look for more nasty combat combos. Try
http://www.niksula.cs.hut.fi/~phartika/games/jyhad/ or
http://members.aol.com/bbretall/jyhad/decks.htm for more ideas. I've
been using alot of these decks with adaptation for the cards I have and
the four card limit I use. Good luck.
